newsitem.title: ITALY: Delay in Italy govt plan not a problem - politicians.
newsitem.headline: Delay in Italy govt plan not a problem - politicians.

text.p: A delay until next week in the Italian cabinet's examination of the government's three-year economic plan (DPEF) is not a major problem, politicians said on Tuesday.

Bruno Solaroli, chairman of the budget commission of the lower house of parliament, told reporters, "The DPEF had been expected to go before the cabinet at the end of this week, but it's only a postponement of a few days."
Earlier, cabinet secretary Enrico Micheli said that the long-awaited programme of rolling targets for 1998-2000 would now be examined by the cabinet early next week.

The document, expected to give indications of savings the government hopes to make from crucial welfare state reforms and including new 1998 deficit forecasts, will be used as the basis for Italy's convergence plan for early membership of the single European currency.
By law, the DPEF should be presented to parliament by May 15 each year following cabinet approval.

"In this case, doing a good job is more important than doing a quick job," said Alfiero Grandi, labour expert of the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS), the main party in Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left coalition.

"A delay of a few days does not cause problems because the most important thing is to come up with positive proposals and for this there is still a need for further discussions within majority parties and with trades unions," he said.

In the last 10 years, only one government has managed to meet the May 15 deadline -- in 1989 the cabinet of prime minister Ciriaco De Mita of the then Christian Democrat party, with Giuliano Amato of the then Socialist party as Treasury Minster, approved the DPEF on May 12 that year.
The longest delay was by the administration headed by Amato in 1992 which did not pass the document until July 31.
